title: Hover and Transitions
story: A pseudo-class like :hover styles an element only in a certain state. A transition makes the change smooth.
goal: Give .btn a :hover rule that changes the background colour, and a transition on .btn.
starter:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>My Page</title>
  <style>
    .btn {
      background: #4ade9f;
      border: 0;
      padding: 10px 18px;
    }
    /* add the hover rule, and a transition on .btn */
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <button class="btn">Play</button>
</body>
</html>

tests.label: There is a .btn:hover rule
tests.js: var rules = []; Array.prototype.forEach.call(document.styleSheets, function (s) { Array.prototype.forEach.call(s.cssRules, function (r) { if (r.selectorText) rules.push(r); }); }); return rules.some(function (r) { return /\.btn:hover/.test(r.selectorText); }) || "no rule for .btn:hover"

tests.label: The hover rule changes the background
tests.js: var ok = false; Array.prototype.forEach.call(document.styleSheets, function (s) { Array.prototype.forEach.call(s.cssRules, function (r) { if (r.selectorText && /\.btn:hover/.test(r.selectorText) && r.style.getPropertyValue("background") + r.style.getPropertyValue("background-color") !== "") ok = true; }); }); return ok || "the :hover rule does not set a background"

tests.label: .btn has a transition
tests.js: var t = css(".btn","transition") + css(".btn","transition-duration"); return (t.replace(/(all 0s ease 0s|0s)/g, "").trim() !== "") || "no transition on .btn"

explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “Hover and Transitions”?
